transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, the main thing that pushed me to come in is that I'm having a lot of trouble just staying at my desk. I process insurance claims for a living, and I keep getting up from my workstation during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to stay put and finish my claim reviews. It's really starting to become a problem.
Have you experienced these difficulties with staying focused or sitting still since you were a child, or is this a more recent development in your life?

Looking back, this isn't really a new thing for me. Um, in elementary school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but I always lost my worksheets. I'd miss instructions a lot, and they constantly had to give me reminders just to finish my regular classwork. So yeah, I guess it's been around for a while.
Would you say that your need to get up from your desk is driven more by a feeling of inner restlessness or a physical urge to move your body?

I think it's more of a physical urge to just move. Um, like, even when I can't get up—say, in trainings or longer team meetings—I’m usually bouncing my leg or clicking my pen. I just end up shifting around in the chair a lot, even when I’m really trying to sit still and look focused.
In your current job, how often do you find yourself making careless mistakes or struggling to maintain focus on the details of those insurance claims?

I don't really know if I make a lot of careless mistakes on the claims, to be honest. I mean, I try to pay attention to the details, but it's hard to say for sure how often I mess up. I haven't really kept track of it.
When you are reviewing those insurance claims, do you find that you frequently lose focus, get distracted by outside noises, or have to re-read things multiple times to understand them?

Yeah, I definitely do. If the people near me start talking about another claim, or even if I just remember some random errand I need to run later, my attention just kind of slides right off what I’m reading. Because of that, I usually end up having to reread the same section a few times just to actually take it in.

When you reflect on your daily struggles, do you feel that the inattention—like getting distracted or having to reread things—is more of a problem for you than the physical urge to move around and fidget?

I'm not entirely sure which one is a bigger problem, honestly. I mean, they both definitely happen a lot, but I haven't really stopped to compare them or figure out which one causes more issues for me day-to-day. They just both kind of get in the way.
When you look back at your childhood, did you struggle as much with sitting still and being physically restless as you did with losing your schoolwork and missing instructions?

I don't really remember, to be honest. I mean, I know I lost my homework a lot and definitely spaced out when teachers were talking, but I can't really say if I was super restless or had trouble sitting still back then. I just don't have a clear memory of comparing the two when I was a kid.
In your daily life, do you often find it difficult to engage in quiet activities or hobbies, or do others ever tell you that you talk too much or seem to be 'on the go' as if driven by a motor?

No, not really. I mean, I like quiet activities, like reading or playing video games, and I don't really have trouble just chilling out. And nobody's ever told me I talk too much or act like I'm driven by a motor. I'm usually pretty quiet, actually.
